QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_12

question.text: In the SPAN margin framework, the scan range represents:

answer.text: The maximum expected price movement of the underlying asset over one trading day, based on a specified confidence level
The range of strike prices available for options
The bid-ask spread of the derivative contract
The range of lot sizes permitted for trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Within SPAN, the "scan range" (also called the price scan range) is the maximum movement in the price of the underlying that the margining system considers over the one-day risk horizon, calibrated to a specified statistical confidence level. SPAN re-prices the portfolio across price changes inside this range together with volatility shifts to estimate the one-day maximum likely loss that initial margin must cover. The Trap: Scan range is not the band of available strike prices, nor the bid-ask spread, nor the range of permissible lot sizes — those are contract specifications, not risk-array inputs to a margin model. Note: The cited NISM-Series-VIII workbook pages (160-161) describe SPAN in terms of the risk array and the one-day maximum likely loss, but the exact term "scan range" with this definition was not located in the pages checked. The framing above reflects general SPAN/clearing-corporation documentation rather than a direct workbook citation.
